newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TRADE DEFICIT TO WORSEN, ANALYSTS PREDICT.
newsitem.headline: TRADE DEFICIT TO WORSEN, ANALYSTS PREDICT.

text.p: The Estonian Institute for Market Research forecast on Thursday that the trade deficit would widen this year and said companies should increase competivity to help bring it down.
Estonia's trade deficit was 13.6 billion kroons last year and the institute predicted that the deficit would grow to 15 billion kroons this year.
A widening current account deficit has also been highlighted. At the end of the third quarter last year, the current account deficit was 852.5 million kroons.

"The most important problem, the trade deficit, is going to increase further this year," Signe Ratso, vice chancellor of the ministry of economy, told a news conference at a presentation of the institute's latest economic survey.
"To raise competitiveness in terms of quality and price could be a solution," Ratso said.
She proposed the establishment of an innovation fund to help with research and development costs and lowering the tax burden for companies as ways the state could achieve that goal.
At the same time, companies themselves have to raise productivity and make cost savings, she added.
The economics ministry is trying to open up new export markets for companies as discussions to sign free trade agreement with Poland and Hungary are going on, Ratso said.
"The ministry is also trying to develop economic relations with Russia," she added.
